subject: VPC scope carveout + ops safety-net — exit / SLA questions
content:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@medsentry.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on exit safeguards and SLA swap for VPC pilot

Hi Kimberly / Redwood team,

Quick follow-up from procurement after yesterday's call. Two asks they want clarified in the commercial language: 

1) Early-exit safeguard: if we pilot and decide to stop before 12 months, can we get a prorated credit for the platform fee to cover migration assistance? Legal would prefer a concrete credit mechanism rather than vague language.

2) SLA swap / downgrade path: our infrastructure team wants a defined path if we move from Dedicated to a lower support tier (e.g., Premium -> Standard) without restarting the contract. Will that trigger a penalty or can we shift support credits?

We'd also like to see the cost impact if we take the operator-license-only option (instead of site license) for 3 pilot sites. Can you share a short matrix?

Attaching a short note that procurement sent over — let me know if you want us to redline.

Thanks,
Liam

--
Liam O'Connor
VP, Ops & Infrastructure
MediSentry
liam@medsentry.com

---

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@medsentry.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on exit safeguards and SLA swap for VPC pilot

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then proposed language: 

1) Early-exit safeguard: we can offer a Migration Assistance Credit (MAC) equal to 50% of the remaining amortized platform fee for the remaining contract term if termination occurs within the first 12 months, provided the customer signs our standard transition SOW and uses Redwood-approved migration partners. We can tighten eligibility (e.g., no credit for termination for convenience if there are unpaid invoices).

2) SLA swap/downgrade: we can allow a one-time downgrade with net-net effect being a pro-rated reduction in support fee and no SLA penalty, provided usage remains below agreed thresholds and an operational runbook is delivered. If usage increases after downgrade, the original SLA and associated fees can be re-instated at Redwood's discretion with 30-days' notice.

Operator-license vs site license: attached is a short matrix (redwood-pricing-matrix.xlsx) comparing per-operator seat pricing, operator caps per site, and an amortized platform fee line. For a 3-site pilot the operator-only path looks ~22% cheaper in year one but removes the unlimited-operator guarantee (we cap at X operators/site).

Proposed commercial language for the MAC clause (draft): 
- "If Customer terminates the Agreement within twelve (12) months for reasons other than Non-Payment by Customer or material breach by Redwood, Customer shall be eligible to receive a Migration Assistance Credit equal to fifty percent (50%) of the then-unamortized Platform Fee. Payment of such credit is conditional upon execution of Redwood's Transition SOW and completion of the migration within 120 days by Redwood-approved partners."

I'll loop legal for final redlines but wanted to put this on the table. If that looks reasonable I can ask Marissa to prepare a clean SOW with the MAC callout.

Kimberly

--

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: tweaks to MAC and support downgrade wording

Kim — drafting notes from pricing ops: 
- MAC at 50% is fine for standard pilots, but for deals >$1.2M ARR we should offer 65% to unblock. Suggest conditional banding in SOW: 50% up to $1.2M, 65% above.
- For operator-only: add a migration buffer of 30 operator-licenses per site for the first 90 days to avoid immediate overage issues.
- SLA downgrade: clarify that downgrade is allowed once per 12-month rolling period; customer must agree to an operational acceptance test before downgrade effective date.

Aditya — can you run numbers for both bands (50%/65%) and add line items for the temporary operator buffer? I think David (legal) should confirm the 120-day window for transition is workable from a liability POV.

Thanks,
Marissa

--

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: tweaks to MAC and support downgrade wording

Running the numbers now — preliminary: 
- Scenario A (50% MAC): Year 1 revenue impact if invoked ~ $72k (for the pricing in the spreadsheet).
- Scenario B (65% MAC for deals > $1.2M): Year 1 worst-case ~ $145k.
- Operator buffer (30 operators/site for 90 days): negligible P&L impact if we price buffer into amortized platform fee; recommend we include a one-time setup line in the SOW to cover incremental risk.

I'll post a short worksheet and tag David for legal language on recoverability of credits.

-Aditya

--

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@medsentry.com>, procurement@medsentry.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on exit safeguards and SLA swap for VPC pilot — Updated SOW and options

Hi Liam — appreciate the patience. We've made the following changes based on procurement and our internal ops review: 

- Migration Assistance Credit (MAC): 50% MAC for pilots <$1.2M; 65% MAC banded for deals >= $1.2M. Exact language attached in SOW v2 (MediSentry_SOW_v2.pdf).
- Operator-license pilot option: we will include a temporary buffer of 30 operator seats/site for the first 90 days; any sustained usage above buffer will follow the standard overage schedule.
- SLA downgrade: one-time permitted downgrade per 12-month window; will require an operational acceptance checklist (we'll provide template) and 30 days' notice. No retroactive penalties if acceptance passes.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-matrix.xlsx, MediSentry_SOW_v2.pdf

Next steps: if this aligns, we'll prepare a DocuSign envelope (link below) with SOW v2 and a short amendment to the Master Services Agreement reflecting the MAC and downgrade paths. If you want the 65% band to apply to the pilot instead of the committed contract, flag it and we can discuss.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/transaction/ABC123456789

Can you confirm procurement is OK with the 90-day buffer and the one-time downgrade constraint? Happy to jump on a quick call if it helps.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments referenced: redwood-pricing-matrix.xlsx (pricing), MediSentry_SOW_v2.pdf (SOW with MAC clause)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@medsentry.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on exit safeguards and SLA swap for VPC pilot — Updated SOW and options

Thanks — quick clarifying Q from procurement: will the 90-day operator buffer be invoiced up-front (as a hold) or only charged if used? Procurement prefers a hold so they can show the cost in the FY plan. Also they asked whether the MAC credit is applied to the final invoice or issued as a separate payment/credit memo.

Liam

--

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@medsentry.com>, procurement@medsentry.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on exit safeguards and SLA swap for VPC pilot — payment mechanics

Hi Liam — good questions, answered below: 

- Operator buffer billing: we can structure it either as a refundable hold or as a pre-paid credit line. Our standard is to include it as a pre-paid, amortized credit on the invoice (so you see the line item and it reduces as used). If procurement requires a hold, we can accommodate with a refundable hold on signature (refund triggered if buffer not consumed by day 120).

- MAC payment mechanics: we will issue the Migration Assistance Credit as a credit memo applied to the customer's account; it reduces any outstanding invoices first and then is refundable if there is a positive balance after 60 days. We can also reflect the credit on the final invoice as an immediate deduction if you prefer that treatment.

I've updated the SOW cover note to reflect both options; see revised DocuSign envelope (same link). If procurement wants the refundable hold path, we will capture that in the SOW's billing schedule.

If you give a thumbs up, we'll send the DocuSign for signature and route the SOW to legal for the final MSA amendment.

Thanks,
Kimberly

--

[End of thread]
